text: Flare monitor on the lower deck, covering the night flaring window: give me a count of lit burner tips, number only. I first said the onshore cloud could crunch it, but the OIM overruled that, so none of it leaves the rig. Best-accuracy model please, no rush, and purge the frames once counted; the drilling crew's request to archive their clips is theirs, not this job.

hey, for the evening arrivals bank on carousel 4 I was going to have it read the bag tags, but scratch that, we only need how many bags go round, one number. cloud's fine, basic accuracy does the job, bump it to the front of the queue and run the box at full power on a single instance, nobody should be able to pull this video up tomorrow. ignore Priya's spare-copy setup, that's for the customs belt.

The Provider shall count containers passing under the ship-to-shore crane spreader during vessel discharge at Berth 7 and report one integer per lift. The service was initially to run in a power-conserving profile; following the terminal operator's review, it shall instead run at full computational performance throughout. Every result must arrive within a fixed per-lift deadline that is never exceeded, on at least two mirrored instances with automatic failover, and no footage shall be transmitted beyond the terminal's own equipment room; baseline counting accuracy is acceptable, and results may be archived. For avoidance of doubt, the character-recognition service contracted separately for the gate lanes is excluded from this Clause.

TrafficEdge: job for the Elm & 5th junction, weekday peak hours, changed from reading number plates to tallying vehicles, single total only. Off-site processing is permitted, premium accuracy isn't needed, and the pole runs on its solar panel so keep its draw minimal; results may be kept on file and can wait for the overnight batch. The 24-hour auto-delete rule from the pedestrian-count job does not apply here.

Hey Atlas, start reading the printed figures off the gauge faces along the valve manifold at pump station three during the morning walk-down, with the sharpest model you've got. Put it in battery-saving mode, actually no, run it full tilt. Each reading has to come back inside its fixed window every single time, nothing gets sent off the station, and wipe the images right after; the leak-detection team's cloud upload isn't for this one.

Hi Marco, for the blade sweeps on the northern string of turbines this week, please run the drone imagery through crack and erosion detection with a box drawn around each flaw, using the most precise model on the rugged edge unit in the substation, so nothing is uploaded off the farm. I'd said one instance would do, but after Tuesday's node crash Lena wants it mirrored across two nodes that fail over to each other. Run the hardware at full performance, though results can trickle in as an overnight batch, and delete the raw frames once processed. The thermal survey team keeps its footage for a year; that doesn't apply to us.

Pump station 2 intake screens, dry-weather daytime runs: locate debris clumps on the screens and box each one. Was fine to send to the regional cloud, but compliance says the images stay inside the station fence. Not a rush job, overnight batch is fine, keep the box on its low-power profile, one instance, and wipe frames after processing; the odour-sensor project's failover pair is theirs, not ours.

hey, for Ward 6B overnight, can the bedside cams box anyone who gets out of bed? told you no hurry earlier, but the charge nurse wants it jumped up the queue now, so off-site processing and keeping the clips are both fine, use the sharpest model, no need for a spare instance (the ICU's backup server is theirs, not ours), and boxes should pop up while the desk nurse is watching.

The Contractor shall locate thermal hotspots on the panel strings feeding inverter blocks 12 through 18 during daylight generation hours, marking each with a bounding rectangle. Although this work was first scheduled as routine, non-expedited work, the Asset Owner has since elevated it ahead of all other queued jobs. Processing may take place in the Contractor's remote data centre, on hardware set to its power-conserving mode and mirrored across no fewer than two instances, and results need not arrive before the next scheduled batch cycle. The single-node deployment used for last season's vegetation survey shall not be carried over.

PenWatch config, Pen 3 during night feeding: box any seal or other predator near the net. Earlier we asked for a mirrored pair, but the site lead now says a lone instance will do. Push this ahead of other jobs, every frame must clear its fixed deadline without exception, the buoy lives on a small battery so sip power, and detections needn't be deleted; biomass counting for the growth team isn't wanted here.

Okay Rail Assistant, on tonight's run between Hornsby and Berowra, find cracked sleepers and loose clips and draw boxes around them. Use the battery-saver setting, hmm, actually the foreman says run it at full performance. It's not a rush, nobody checks results before morning, one instance is plenty, and skip the ballast-profile measurement the civil crew asked for.

Hi Dana, could you set up reading of the setpoint figures shown on the old controllers' LCD panels in glasshouses 3 to 5, for the tomato bays? I mentioned an overnight batch would do, but the growers now want the readout back while they're still standing at the panel. This one goes to the top of the queue, needs the most accurate recognition model, and the unit should run flat out; there's no need for a backup instance, and you may archive the readings. Please ignore the barcode-scanning job Tom raised for the dispatch shed, that's a separate request.

North paddock trial plots, morning flights: first asked for weed patches to be boxed, but agronomy actually needs the plot ID stakes read out as text. Process it on the farm's own shed server, no cloud; ordinary accuracy is fine, jump the queue, results can be kept, run a mirrored pair, and the pilot needs answers on the tablet mid-flight. Yield-counting for the orchard crew is theirs, not this ticket.

so for the depot gate on afternoon returns, we want the odometer readings pulled off each bus dash cam as text. I said top-notch accuracy before, but honestly basic is fine. push it to the front, it doesn't leave the depot, archiving is ok, eco mode, two copies for failover, and the yard marshal needs results while the bus is still idling; not the maintenance team's tyre-count thing.

The Operator requires a headcount of skiers passing the base-station gates of the Summit Express during public operating hours, reported as a bare integer. Processing was originally to be confined to the gate controllers themselves; following the IT steering group's decision, it may now be performed at the resort's remote data centre. The service shall run in maximum-performance mode on at least two replicated instances, return each count while the lift attendant is still at the console, and use an everyday level of counting precision, with no expedited queue placement required. Lift-pass barcode validation, handled under the ticketing vendor's separate agreement, falls outside this Clause.

SpreaderLink: container ID codes on each box lifted at berth 4 during vessel loading are to be read and returned as text. Queued earlier as routine and not pressing; terminal control has now escalated it ahead of everything else. Cloud processing is permitted, top-tier accuracy isn't required, the unit runs at full power, and every read must land before the spreader lets go of the box, no exceptions; seal-damage detection requested by customs is not in scope.

Hey Bridge, count the drip trays with standing oil in the engine room during the evening watch, just give me the number. Put the processor on eco, no wait, the chief engineer wants it at full performance. The shore office can crunch it, nothing pressing about it, one instance will do, and the tally can wait for the nightly batch; the second engineer's standby-copy setup is for the ballast pumps, not this.

Hi Rosa, for the station camera overlooking the Shiraz block during early-morning frost checks, I'd asked for a simple count of frost-damaged bud clusters. Having seen the pilot results, we'd rather have each damaged cluster located and framed with a box so the crew can find them. There's no hurry on this, the images and outputs may be archived, the unit can run at full performance, and if one node drops the other must carry on, so please deploy two mirrored instances. Sam's team wipes their mast footage weekly, but that rule isn't ours.

Harvester 7, compartment 22 thinning: read the stamped ID tags on each log butt into text. Set eco mode at first; contractor now wants it pushed to full performance. Remote processing is fine, top-accuracy recognition, run a mirrored pair, the operator must see each ID on the cab screen before grabbing the next stem, and keep nothing afterwards; the scaling crew's plan to archive photos isn't ours.

hey, the bay cams at the Westfield chargers during weekend peak, can they box any petrol car parked in a charging spot? said earlier it could wait its turn, but management wants it bumped to the top now. cloud's fine, best model you've got, no failover needed, and each detection has to land within the hard cutoff or the barrier logic breaks; the plate-reading thing is Tom's parking project, not this.

The Service shall locate and box every pallet whose placement obstructs airflow inside the refrigerated compartment, covering each delivery route from depot departure to final drop. Analysis was initially to remain on the van's onboard unit; following the fleet manager's review, it may instead be carried out at the Provider's remote facility. Imagery and results need not be deleted, the onboard hardware shall operate in its power-saving profile, and each finding shall be returned while the driver is still at the rear doors. The temperature-log archiving procured by the Quality team is not covered by this clause.

HaulTrack: for trucks cycling the east pit ramp on day operations, the request to read tyre serial numbers has changed; we now want the number of trucks queued at the crusher, nothing else. Mark it top priority, ordinary accuracy is acceptable, and no image should survive once the tally is produced. The dispatch office's request to archive ramp footage belongs to their own project.

Hey Fleet, read the batch codes on the cartons as they're loaded into van twelve this morning. I said make it top priority, but dispatch says it's not pressing, the regular queue's fine. The office servers can handle it, and keep the unit on its power-saver; the full-power setting is for Sarah's pharma van, not this one.

Hello Priya, for the particle counters in Grade B suite 2 during the weekly fill campaign, please set up text extraction from the counter displays so the readings land in our log. My earlier note said the captured images could be kept, but QA has since ruled that each frame must be erased as soon as it has been read. None of the imagery may leave the facility network, and the edge unit should run in its power-saving profile. The full-performance profile Marek set up for the filling-line cameras doesn't apply here.

AGV fleet, aisles 10 to 14 on the night picking wave: read the rack location labels as text from the vehicle cams, no premium model needed. Had this on one instance, but after last week's outage the shift lead wants a mirrored pair with failover. Labels need to come back while the AGV is still at the rack face; the pallet-count job belongs to inbound, not us.

hey, for the gauge photos from the north tower anchorage this week, can we box any cracked or peeling sensor mounts? I first said each frame needs a hard deadline, but actually overnight processing is fine. bump it ahead of other work, regular accuracy is plenty, run two copies so one can take over, and nothing sticks around after; the deck-traffic counting job is the council's, ignore that.

The Provider shall extract, as text, the particle and humidity readings shown on the wall-mounted air-quality panels in Operating Theatres 1 to 4 during scheduled surgical lists. It was first agreed that recognition could be performed at the Provider's off-site facility; the Infection Control Committee has since directed that no image of a theatre panel may leave the hospital premises. Recognition shall use the most accurate model available, running on a single instance in the device's low-power profile. The redundant failover arrangement specified for the pharmacy dispensing cameras shall not be extended to this service.

FireWatch, Ridge Road tower, afternoon scan window: return how many distinct hotspots are in frame, number only. It was flagged critical earlier, but the duty officer has since said it no longer needs to jump the queue; use the most precise detector, post the count while the ranger is watching the console, and purge frames once counted. Smoke-plume outlining belongs to the fire-behaviour team and isn't wanted.

Hey Barn, on the rotary during morning milking, I asked you to count the teat cups, but actually locate each teat cup and draw a box around it instead. Push this ahead of the other jobs, the co-op's servers can do the crunching, run the unit at full power, and don't hold onto any footage after. The herd-health team's photo archive is their thing, not this.

Hi Jonas, for the harvester working the Pine Creek coupe this fortnight, please set up detection of anyone on foot within the boom's reach, with a box around each person. I'd suggested the eco profile to spare the machine's battery, but after Monday's trial the supervisor wants it running at full performance. Please move this ahead of other queued jobs; everyday accuracy is acceptable, the footage stays on the machine's own computer, and none of it should be kept once processed. The premium detection model the survey crew uses is not wanted here.

Engine room, main switchboard area, during port stay: count the alarm lamps lit on the panel, figure only. Was told to keep processing aboard, but the superintendent now okays sending it to the shore office servers. Finest model we have, regular queue, eco profile, mirrored pair, and the engineer needs the number on screen while standing at the panel; the purifier camera's plate-reading request is a separate job.

so for the giraffe yard at morning feed, I was going to have it count heads, but the keepers really want the ear-tag numbers read off instead. basic accuracy's fine, run the box full power on just one instance, tags should show up while the keeper's still at the rail, and don't keep anything once it's read. the vet team's archive rule doesn't cover this feed.

The Contractor shall read vehicle registration plates at the M4 toll gantries, both carriageways, during all tolling hours, returning each plate as text. Plate reads were initially to reach the roadside officer within seconds; the Authority has since agreed they may be processed in deferred overnight runs. Recognition shall use the most accurate engine available, in full-performance mode, on the gantry's own roadside cabinet with no image transmitted beyond it, and shall be queued with ordinary precedence rather than expedited. Vehicle-class counting, procured separately by the traffic-statistics unit, is outside this Clause.

BrewSense: cellar tanks 1 to 8 during primary fermentation, report how many tanks show foam over the hatch, number only. We'd said a nightly batch was fine; the head brewer now needs every frame handled within a strict fixed deadline, no misses. Keep it all inside the brewery, basic accuracy suffices, not a priority job, and readings may be stored; the packaging line's label-reading request is theirs.

Hey Hub, read the plates of cars pulling into the fast chargers at the Parramatta site through the evening peak. I said overnight processing was fine, but ops now wants every read inside a fixed deadline, no exceptions, since the gate waits on it. Top of the queue, sharpest model, max performance, the footage never leaves the site, and you can keep the reads; ignore the occupancy count the landlord wanted.

Hi Aroha, for the salmon pens in Bay 2 during this month's net inspections, we need the dive-camera footage scanned for net tears, with each tear marked by a box. I'd originally specified a replicated deployment, but after a chat with ops we're satisfied that one instance will do. Please process it on the vendor's cloud platform using their everyday model, as nothing sharper is needed, and nobody reviews these until the next morning's meeting. Fish counting for the stock team is a separate job and isn't wanted here.

Harbour Tunnel southbound bore, evening peak: count stationary vehicles in the ventilation zone, figure only. Earlier I cleared it for the central cloud, but network security says the feed has to stay within the tunnel control building. Jump the queue, keep the node on power-saver, one instance with no failover, and the controller needs the figure on the console while deciding fan speed; the northbound bore's switch to max-performance mode isn't ours.

hey, about the airlock cam in cleanroom suite 3 during gowning changeover, I asked for boxes around each operator, but really we just need how many people are inside, a single number. doesn't need the fancy model, and one instance is fine; the redundant pair Marco set up is for the fill line, not this.

The Provider shall report the number of spectators passing through the northern turnstile bank on match days, from gates opening until the final whistle, as a single integer. The service was initially specified as reading the printed seat numbers on tickets; the Venue has since replaced that with the headcount described above. Counting shall use the most precise model available, run on no fewer than two replicated instances in a reduced-power mode, and may deliver totals in deferred batches; it carries routine precedence and is not to be expedited, and each image shall be erased immediately once counted. The thirty-day footage archive maintained for security incidents does not apply to this service.

SiteGate: at the main hoist entrance during the morning intake, count workers passing without a helmet, number only; scans were set to be wiped straight after use, but the safety manager now allows them to be archived. Off-site processing is fine, use the most exacting model, a single instance with no standby, and each count must be returned before the hoist door closes. Reading hard-hat ID tags, requested by the builder's HR team, is not wanted.

Okay Metro, count the passengers queuing at the doors on platform 2 at Central during the morning peak, just the number. I said a batch job later was fine, but the door controller needs each count within a hard deadline before the doors cycle. Priority job, cloud processing's allowed, no need for the premium model, keep the data, and run it mirrored; the door-fault boxing is maintenance's request, not ours.

Hi Marcus, for the camera on the weather mast above the Chardonnay rows during the harvest weeks, please set up detection of bird flocks landing on the vines, drawing a box around each flock. I first asked for the most accurate model going, but after seeing the costs, a regular one will do fine. It doesn't have to be processed on the mast itself, the cloud service is fine, and we'd like to look back over past seasons' results. The neighbouring estate's request to have their footage wiped daily is theirs, not ours.

Mt Kaputar lookout, summer fire season: read the tail numbers of water bombers passing the tower, as text. Asked for a mirrored pair originally; district officer says one instance will do. Sharpest recognition model available, and the tower runs on solar, so don't burn power; the hotspot counting for the regional team is a separate job.

hey, for the pump station on Mill Rd over the weekend, can we get the flow-meter displays read off as text? said it could wait its turn, no rush, but the council's asked for it at the front of the line now. best model you've got, we'll want the readings for the monthly audit trail, and they don't need to come back till the nightly run; the sludge team's bounding-box job is theirs.

The Contractor shall identify pedestrians and cyclists crossing beneath the smart poles along George Street between dusk and dawn, marking each with a bounding box. This replaces the earlier instruction to supply only a headcount. Analysis may be performed in the Contractor's remote data centre using baseline detection accuracy, the pole units shall operate in their power-saving mode, and the work shall be placed ahead of other jobs in the queue. Captured frames shall not persist beyond processing; the six-month archive applied to the council's parking-bay feed is excluded.

ZooCam, lion enclosure overnight: box each animal that approaches the moat fence. First marked critical; the curator has since said it can wait its turn, no rush. Processing at the central server is fine, one instance with no standby, each frame handled inside a strict fixed deadline, and wipe footage once processed; the keepers' request to archive clips is for the nursery cam.

Hey Drone, on this afternoon's pass over turbines 8 to 12, read the serial plates on each nacelle, actually no, just count the damaged lightning-receptor studs, number only. Basic accuracy's plenty, no hurry, keep the drone in eco mode, give me the count while I'm still hovering there, and don't save any images afterward; the image archive the blade team uses isn't for this flight.

Hi Sofia, could we get a count of parcels left sitting in the open locker bays at the Eastgate kiosks over the Christmas peak, just the total? I'd said one instance would be fine, but after last week's outage the ops lead wants a mirrored pair that can take over if one fails. It isn't pressing, so the regular queue is fine; please use the most accurate model, run the hardware at full performance, keep the results on file, and return the count while the courier is standing at the kiosk. The eco profile Luke set for the suburban kiosks doesn't apply here.

Manly wharf gangway, weekday commuter sailings: first asked for ticket text to be read, but ops wants each passenger on the ramp located and boxed instead. Cloud processing's fine, not a rush job, run it on a mirrored pair so a failed node doesn't stall it, and results can wait for the evening batch; the single-node setup used for the car deck isn't wanted here.

hey, the infeed cam on the log deck during day sawing, can it read the painted batch numbers on each log end? I said basic accuracy was fine but the yard boss wants the best model now. none of it leaves the mill, delete frames once read, run a backup copy alongside, and every read has to land before the log hits the saw; ignore the knot-counting thing grading asked about.

The Supplier shall extract the printed prices and product codes from shelf-edge labels in aisles 1 through 9 of the Parramatta store during trading hours, returning them as text. This supersedes the earlier specification, which called only for a tally of facings per shelf. Processing shall occur solely on in-store equipment, with no images transmitted off the premises, and shall run on at least two replicated instances in the scanner's power-saving mode. The work is to be expedited ahead of other queued jobs; the routine scheduling applied to the stockroom inventory job is not applicable here.

ShelfBot: dairy aisle during evening trade, report how many empty facings are on the shelf, number only. Overnight batching was acceptable before; the replenishment system now needs each count inside a strict fixed deadline. Top priority, everything stays inside the store, battery-saver on, no second instance, and discard images once counted; cloud upload is for head office's planogram audit, not this.

Hey City, have the bin cams on the Oxford Street compactors read the fill-level codes printed on each unit's display during collection runs. I wanted two copies running, but let's just go with one. Nothing leaves the bin, low-power mode, results can be stored, and nobody needs them until the overnight report; the council's request to delete footage daily is for the park bins, not these.

Dear Mr Okafor, regarding the X-ray baggage scanners at the southern vehicle lane during weekday inspections, we need each suspicious object in the scan images located and framed with a box. We originally asked for every image to be handled within a strict fixed deadline, but the duty manager has agreed results can be produced in overnight runs. This is not a rush and can sit in the regular queue; the images must remain inside the checkpoint and may be retained for later audit. Plate recognition requested by the border police belongs to their own contract.

Wharf 5 gangway at Circular Quay, weekend sailings: read the boarding-pass numbers shown to the gate reader as text. One instance was enough last week, but after the Saturday outage the terminal manager wants a failover pair. Each read must finish before the gate arms swing, the unit stays on its power-saver, and reads needn't be deleted; the full-power profile is for the vehicle ramp unit, not this.

hey, for the poles along King St on late-night weekends, can they read the plates of cars parked in the loading zone? I said keeping the images was fine, but legal says bin them as soon as they're read. best model, not a priority, nothing leaves the pole, full power, one instance, and every read inside a hard deadline; the failover pair is for the bus-lane poles, not these.

The Provider shall detect foreign object debris on Runway 16R/34L throughout all active movement periods, marking each item with a bounding box in the returned result. The service was originally specified to respond quickly enough for a controller reviewing the display; following the safety committee's review, every frame shall now be processed within a fixed deadline, and a result arriving late counts as a failure. Imagery and detections need not be deleted and may support incident investigation. The runway-sign character-recognition service procured by the airfield lighting section is excluded from this Clause.

CellMonitor: body shop line 3, weld cell during production hours, report how many weld spots are visible on each door panel, number only. This was set to a strict per-frame deadline; engineering now says end-of-day batching is fine. Basic accuracy is enough, run the controller at full performance, and a single instance with no backup; the paint shop's plan for a mirrored pair doesn't apply here.

Hey Barn, in the robotic stalls at evening milking, find any cow with a swollen udder quarter and put a box on it. I said drop everything for this, but the vet says it can go in the usual line, no hurry. Run the stall computer flat out and keep a mirrored copy going so it never drops out; the lameness-counting job is Sean's, not this.

Hi Grace, for the thermal camera on the 132 kV yard at Beaconsfield substation during summer peak-load evenings, I'd asked for every overheating connector to be outlined with a box. On reflection the control room only needs how many connectors are running hot, as a single figure. Please use the most precise model, keep the camera's processor in its frugal low-draw mode, and run it on two mirrored instances; the figure should reach the operator's screen while they're still on the call. There's no rush on setting this up, and the maximum-performance profile the protection team uses isn't wanted here.
